title: Sync planner and conflict resolver tests
name: Sync engine test suite

questions.prompt: Is there a defect in how these tests check that the chunk plan covers the whole file? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.

The table in `splitsAroundChunkBoundaries` (chunk size 4) includes sizes 4 and 8 as well as 3, 5 and 9. Which faulty implementation of the chunk count would be caught by the sizes 4 and 8 and by no other row?
choices: Always returning 1 chunk for sizes up to 8

questions.prompt: `resolvesEachScenario` and `swappingSidesMirrorsTheOutcome` both use `@MethodSource("cases")`. What does sharing the provider buy?
choices: It makes the two tests run in parallel on the same data
It avoids creating FileVersion objects twice, which would be slow
Every new row added to the table is automatically checked in both orientations, and the second test needs no expected values of its own
It lets the second test skip the cases whose outcome is KEEP_BOTH

questions.prompt: `SyncConflictResolver` takes a `Clock` and the test builds it with `Clock.fixed(NOW, ...)`. What does this make possible in `clockSkewWithinToleranceIsAccepted` and `timestampBeyondToleranceIsRejected`?
choices: The 4-minute and 6-minute timestamps sit at known distances from the resolver's notion of now, so the tolerance boundary is tested deterministically
The tests can run on any time zone without conversion because ZoneOffset.UTC is used
The resolver caches the current time, which speeds up repeated calls
The tests no longer need the 5 minute tolerance to be configurable
